title: needs_refetch returns False when nothing was ever drawn, so ticking Show neighbourhood no longer draws it after an 'off' Draw or a fully failed fetch
detail: The round-1 fix took out the 'nothing held for this document -> fetch' branch and replaced it with 'a live-only layer in the record and nothing held'. When there is no record, `layers` is [] and the function returns any([]) = False. A file has no record in two normal cases. (1) sync_context step 'off': the architect did a Draw with Show neighbourhood unticked; `_clear_context(doc)` deletes the record and Gordium says 'Neighbourhood not drawn: Show neighbourhood is off in the panel (tick it to draw it).' (2) The first fetch failed outright (offline, timeout, error): sync step 'draw' already cleared, and draw_context returns before it writes a record; on a timeout the message says '(Show neighbourhood tries again)'. In both cases show_context(True) now computes refetch=False, only makes the empty layers visible, and says 'Neighbourhood shown (drawing only: the check never measures it).' Nothing is fetched and nothing is drawn. Before this change guides_of(None) was False, so it returned True and fetched. The architect does what the message tells them and gets nothing, plus a message saying the neighbourhood is shown.
evidence:
rhino_logic.needs_refetch:
    layers = list(((record or {}).get("layers") or {}).values())
    if any(not is_stored(v) for v in layers) and not guides_of(held, doc_serial):
        return True
    return any((v or {}).get("status") not in DREW for v in layers)
Ran: needs_refetch(None, None, 1) -> False; needs_refetch({'doc':1,'lines':[]}, None, 1) -> False.
gordium_rhino.show_context: `refetch = logic.needs_refetch(...)`; `if on and refetch: ... draw_context(...)` / `elif on: ... say("Neighbourhood shown (drawing only: the check never measures it).")`.
gordium_rhino._context_payload timeout: "...the lot is drawn without it (Show neighbourhood tries again)."
sync_context: `elif step == "off": say("Neighbourhood not drawn: Show neighbourhood is off in the panel (tick it to draw it).")` after `_clear_context(doc)` (which runs doc.Strings.Delete(SECTION, logic.CONTEXT_ENTRY)).
Old (493db79): `if not guides_of(held, doc_serial): return True`.
pin: packages/design_checker/tests/test_context_box.py: a new test asserting that with no record there is something to fetch: `assert logic.needs_refetch(None, None, DOC)` and `assert logic.needs_refetch({"doc": DOC, "lines": []}, None, DOC)`, with the kept-footprints test (`not logic.needs_refetch(None, record, DOC)` for a stored record that worked) still passing. Today the new assertion fails.
suggested_fix: In needs_refetch, return True when the record has no layers (nothing drawn for this lot: `if not layers: return True`), then apply the live-only and failed-layer rules. sync_context cannot loop on this: its refetch branch needs step == 'keep' with a frame, which means a record with the same frame exists.
skeptics:
I could not refute this; the finding holds. In packages/design_checker/design_checker/rhino_logic.py:1502-1513, needs_refetch builds `layers` from `record` and returns `any(...)` over that list. When there is no record the list is empty and the function returns False. I ran it: needs_refetch(None,None,1) gives False, and needs_refetch({'doc':1,'lines':[]},None,1) gives False.

A missing record does happen in the plugin, in the two cases the finding names. Both are in apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py:
(1) The 'off' step. sync_context (2619-2648) calls `_clear_context(doc)` for step 'off'. _clear_context (2446-2490) runs `doc.Strings.Delete(SECTION, logic.CONTEXT_ENTRY)` when sources is None, and also drops context_guides. Then it says '...(tick it to draw it).'
(2) A first fetch that failed. Step 'draw' clears first. Then draw_context (2560-2566) returns early when `payload.get('status') != 'found'`, before `doc.Strings.SetString(...)`, so no record is written. The timeout message at 2535 says '(Show neighbourhood tries again)'.

In both cases show_context (2663-2687) computes refetch=False, so draw_context is never called. It takes the `elif on:` branch and says 'Neighbourhood shown (drawing only: the check never measures it).' Nothing is fetched or drawn.

The version at 493db79 started with `if not guides_of(held, doc_serial): return True`, which fetched in this situation, so this is a regression inside the PR. Base 5937781 has no show_context, so this is not a pre-existing issue. I found no upstream guarantee that a record exists when the box is ticked.

I tried to refute this and couldn't. The finding holds.

1. The function: packages/design_checker/design_checker/rhino_logic.py:1502-1513, needs_refetch. When there is no record, `layers` is []. The first branch needs any() over that list, which is False. The function then returns any([]), also False. I ran it on the branch: `needs_refetch(None, None, 1)` returns False. The old code was `if not guides_of(held, doc_serial): return True`, so it returned True here. The change came in a66fe49, which is inside 5937781..c783ee6, so this PR introduced it.

2. The record really is missing in the two cases named:
   - apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py:2489-2492: `_clear_context(doc)` with no `sources` pops `context_guides` and runs `doc.Strings.Delete(SECTION, CONTEXT_ENTRY)`.
   - sync_context (2619-2645): on step "off" or "draw" it calls `_clear_context(doc)` first.
   - draw_context (2555-2565): when the payload status is not "found" (a timeout, an error, or a partial result) it returns before `doc.Strings.SetString` (~2600). So a first fetch that fails leaves no record.

3. The tick: show_context (2663-2685) computes `refetch = needs_refetch(...)`, which is False. It goes to `elif on:` and says "Neighbourhood shown (drawing only: the check never measures it)." without fetching. That contradicts the off-step message at 2639 ("tick it to draw it") and the timeout message at ~2534 ("Show neighbourhood tries again").

4. No upstream guard: nothing writes a record or holds guides in those paths before the tick. A later box Draw would still fetch, because context_step(frame, None, on) gives "draw". But the tick, the action the message points to, does nothing. The finding is real.

title: Edit detection misses common architect edits: print width/colour, material, group, and a copy pasted in place are deleted on redraw/clear
detail: Ben's rule (2026-10-21) is that Gordium removes only outlines it drew and the architect hasn't edited. The fingerprint covers points (with Z), name, display colour, linetype and the architect's own user text. It leaves out other attributes architects routinely set on context linework: PlotWeight and PlotWeightSource (lineweight for a sheet), PlotColor and PlotColorSource, MaterialIndex and MaterialSource, and group membership (GetGroupList). A footprint whose print width was changed, or that was grouped with the architect's own linework, still matches its fingerprint. On the next clear (another address, Show-off Draw, sources None) or same-lot redraw it is deleted by `doc.Objects.Delete(o, True)` and, around the same lot, drawn again without the edit. A copy pasted in place (Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V) carries the original's GEOM_KEY and CONTEXT_KEY with identical points and attributes, so it is deleted too. Yet DRAWN_KEY != its own id already proves it is the architect's copy: `suppressed` uses exactly that signal, but `_clear_context` does not.
evidence:
_attrs_print returns only {"name", "colour_source", "colour", "linetype_source", "linetype", "user"}.
_clear_context:
    if logic.is_edited(o.Attributes.GetUserString(logic.GEOM_KEY), _outline_points(o.Geometry),
                       _attrs_print(o.Attributes)):
        ... EDITED_KEY ...
    else:
        doc.Objects.Delete(o, True)
There is no check of `o.Attributes.GetUserString(logic.DRAWN_KEY) != str(o.Id)` in _clear_context; rhino_logic.suppressed already relies on `e.get("drawn_as") == e.get("own")`.
pin: test_context_box.py: extend test_an_outline_the_architect_edited_is_known_and_never_drawn_twice with `assert logic.is_edited(key, drawn, dict(attrs, plot_weight=0.5))` and a group change, and a source assertion that _attrs_print reads attrs.PlotWeight, attrs.PlotColor, attrs.MaterialIndex and attrs.GetGroupList(). Add a source-level assertion that _clear_context treats `GetUserString(logic.DRAWN_KEY) != str(o.Id)` as the architect's (kept, EDITED_KEY set) before Delete.
suggested_fix: Add PlotColorSource/PlotColor, PlotWeightSource/PlotWeight, MaterialSource/MaterialIndex and the sorted group list to _attrs_print (one place, so draw and clear agree). In _clear_context, keep any outline whose DRAWN_KEY is not its own id (a copy is the architect's) without comparing fingerprints. Put both decisions in a rhino_logic helper so they can be tested.
skeptics: I read apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py:2436-2443. `_attrs_print` returns only name, colour_source, colour, linetype_source, linetype and the architect's own user text. It leaves out PlotWeight/PlotWeightSource, PlotColor/PlotColorSource, MaterialIndex/MaterialSource and group membership. At 2446-2483, `_clear_context` decides only through `logic.is_edited(GEOM_KEY, points, _attrs_print(...))`. If that is false it calls `doc.Objects.Delete(o, True)`, and it never compares DRAWN_KEY with o.Id. In packages/design_checker/design_checker/rhino_logic.py:1660-1667, `suppressed` already uses `drawn_as == own` to tell the outline Gordium drew from a copy, and its docstring says a copy "carries the original's user text under a new id". So the codebase itself expects copies to carry GEOM_KEY and CONTEXT_KEY. A copy pasted in place has the same points and the same printed attributes, so `is_edited` returns false and the copy is deleted. The same happens to a footprint whose only change is its print width, material or group. Its fingerprint still matches, so it is deleted and then drawn again (draw_context 2557-2600) without the edit. That breaks the rule quoted in is_edited's docstring (Ben, 2026-10-21: only unedited outlines Gordium drew are removed). This is new code in this PR: on 5937781 there are no matches for `_attrs_print`, `is_edited` or `DRAWN_KEY`. I found no earlier check that stops any of this, such as a filter on group or plot weight. The finding holds.

I tried to refute this and couldn't. The finding holds, and the code is new in this PR: 5937781 has no _attrs_print.

1. The fingerprint leaves those attributes out. gordium_rhino.py:2436-2443: _attrs_print returns only name, colour_source, colour, linetype_source, linetype and the user's non-gordium_ user strings. rhino_logic.py:1634-1650 (outline_key / is_edited) hashes only those points and that dict. So a change to PlotWeight or PlotWeightSource, PlotColor or PlotColorSource, MaterialIndex or MaterialSource, or group membership leaves the fingerprint unchanged, and is_edited returns False.

2. Such an outline is deleted. gordium_rhino.py:2474-2482: in _clear_context, an outline that is not "edited" goes to doc.Objects.Delete(o, True). Nothing upstream stops this: the only test is that CONTEXT_KEY is present and in `sources`.

3. A copy pasted in place is deleted too. The copy carries the original's user text: GEOM_KEY, CONTEXT_KEY and the DRAWN_KEY set at 2596-2599. Its points and attributes are identical, so is_edited is False and it is deleted. The Buildings layer stays unlocked, so the paste can land there (_lock_context and the section comment at about 2400).

4. The code already has the signal to tell a copy apart. rhino_logic.suppressed (1660-1667) checks drawn_as == own to tell a copy from the original. _clear_context never compares DRAWN_KEY with str(o.Id).

5. After a same-lot redraw, the outline is drawn again without the edit. draw_context (about 2575-2600) calls _clear_context, then draws everything skip_edited lets through. The deleted object never got EDITED_KEY, so its id is not suppressed.

This breaks the stated rule at rhino_logic.py:1646-1648 that an outline the architect edited stays.

title: In-Rhino evidence predates the editable outlines; the new Rhino-only claims (parent unlocked, footprints selectable, lifted outline kept, solid row needs review) were never run
detail: context_in_rhino.py now asserts claims that only Rhino can prove: a locked parent blocks selecting sublayer objects, `Objects.Transform` keeps the object id (which `suppressed` depends on), int() of the pythonnet enums in _attrs_print works, the fingerprint round-trips, and the run's state is needs_review with the 'neighbourhood layers' row. The only recorded run is the 11-claim one from b8322b6/b908e99: '2 The building footprints are on screen | 212 footprints, shown live' and '5 A saved file keeps no live-only source'. Neither 493db79 nor a66fe49 touched docs/evidence. CI covers only the string- and logic-level halves, so the PR's 'how we know it is right' for the round-1 P0/P1 fixes rests on an unrun script.
evidence: `git diff --stat 493db79..c783ee6` lists no docs/evidence files. context_results.json claims: ['1 the neighbourhood is drawn on its own locked, grey layers...', '2 the building footprints are on screen (live: claim 5 checks they are never saved)', ..., '5 a saved file keeps no live-only (store: none) source', ...]. It has no 'parent_unlocked', 'selectable', 'lifted_kept_once' or 'solid_check' keys, while context_in_rhino.py now builds log["footprints"]["parent_unlocked"], log["edited"]["lifted_kept_once"] and log["solid_check"].
pin: An evidence run at the branch head adds a dated context_results.json beside the old one with every claim true. A test in test_context_box.py (like the existing evidence-names-the-commit checks) asserts the newest evidence JSON contains the 'solid_check', 'parent_unlocked' and 'lifted_kept_once' keys.
suggested_fix: Run apps/rhino_plugin/tests/context_in_rhino.py in Rhino 8 at the branch head and add the results and README section beside the dated earlier run (do not edit the old record). The PR's Test Plan should cite that run for the P0 (needs-review row) and P1 (parent unlocked, Z/attribute edits kept) fixes.
skeptics: I could not refute this. `git diff --stat 493db79..c783ee6` lists 12 files and none of them are under docs/evidence. `git log 5937781..c783ee6 -- docs/evidence` shows the last evidence commits are 04770a9 (the tick run at 64d1425) and b8322b6/f092f44 (the 11-claim run at b908e99), all older than 493db79 (editable outlines) and a66fe49 (review round 1). apps/rhino_plugin/tests/context_in_rhino.py now builds log["footprints"]["parent_unlocked"] (line 184), log["edited"]["lifted_kept_once"] (line 219) and log["solid_check"], and asserts that the state is needs_review with a 'neighbourhood layers' row (lines 241-244). grep finds 0 of those keys in docs/evidence/pr-23/context_results.json. docs/evidence/pr-23/README.md still records claim 2 as '212 footprints, shown live' and claim 5 as 'No footprint (store: none) in the saved .3dm'. Both describe the old live-only footprints, not the editable outlines this PR now ships. The README says it is a dated record and that 'a later run is added beside it', but no later run was added. So the evidence for the Rhino-only half of the round-1 fixes does not exist, and the finding holds.

The finding holds. I checked it in the review_pr23 checkout.

(1) `git log -- docs/evidence/pr-23` shows the last evidence commits are 04770a9, 64d1425 and f092f44. All three come before 493db79 (the editable-footprints feature) and a66fe49 (the round-1 fix). `git diff --stat 493db79..c783ee6` lists no docs/evidence files.

(2) docs/evidence/pr-23/README.md lines 7-9 and the claims table give the run as context_in_rhino.py at b8322b6 with the plugin at b908e99, 11 of 11. The table still states the old behaviour: claim 2 is "212 footprints, shown live" and claim 5 is "No footprint (store: none) in the saved .3dm".

(3) The diff to apps/rhino_plugin/tests/context_in_rhino.py (38d19d5..c783ee6) rewrites claim 1 ("locked but for the footprints") and claim 2 (log["footprints"] with parent_unlocked and selectable). It adds the drag/lift claim (log["edited"]["lifted_kept_once"], which depends on the object id surviving Objects.Transform) and the solid claim (log["solid_check"] must be needs_review with a 'neighbourhood layers' reason).

(4) Grepping context_results.json for parent_unlocked, selectable, lifted_kept_once and solid_check finds 0 matches.

So the Rhino-only claims that the round-1 P0/P1 fixes rely on have never been run, and the recorded evidence describes the behaviour those commits replaced. One mitigating point: the README calls itself a dated record that is never changed and names b8322b6 explicitly, so it isn't wrong as a historical record. But no newer run sits beside it, so for this PR's current claims the gap is real.
